```{r}
#| label: setup

locate_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (
      file.exists(file.path(candidate, "renv.lock")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(
          candidate,
          "preregistration",
          "AsPredicted #273407.pdf"
        ))
    ) {
      return(candidate)
    }
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) {
      stop("Could not locate the Nature Health project root", call. = FALSE)
    }
    candidate <- parent
  }
}

range_cell <- function(value, digits = 0L) {
  limits <- range(value, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (isTRUE(all.equal(limits[[1L]], limits[[2L]]))) {
    return(formatC(limits[[1L]], digits = digits, format = "f"))
  }
  paste0(
    formatC(limits[[1L]], digits = digits, format = "f"),
    "–",
    formatC(limits[[2L]], digits = digits, format = "f")
  )
}

format_ci <- function(estimate, lower, upper, digits = 3L) {
  paste0(
    formatC(estimate, digits = digits, format = "fg", flag = "#"),
    " (",
    formatC(lower, digits = digits, format = "fg", flag = "#"),
    " to ",
    formatC(upper, digits = digits, format = "fg", flag = "#"),
    ")"
  )
}
```

# Result at the Stage 2 gate

The signed hypothesis is:

> **H7: There is a ceiling (nonlinear) effect of absolute latitude and
> photoperiod on level-, duration-, and exposure-history-based light metrics.**

::: {.callout-note title="Answer in brief"}
Under the owner-revised pointwise derivative rule, six of nine primary
near-eye metrics show a derivative-defined plateau pattern: mean melEDI,
brightest and darkest 10 h means, time above 1,000 lx melEDI, time above 250 lx
melEDI during wake, and melEDI dose. The six transition brackets range from
14.24–14.35 h to 16.10–16.20 h. Time below 10 lx melEDI before sleep and time
below 1 lx melEDI during sleep have no earlier pointwise detected increase;
the derivative for longest continuous period above 250 lx melEDI remains
pointwise positive at the recorded upper boundary.

Seven of nine complementary chest metrics meet the same rule, with transitions
bracketed from 13.01–13.11 h to 18.36–18.47 h. Brightest 10 h mean remains
pointwise positive at the recorded upper boundary, and time below 10 lx melEDI
before sleep has no earlier detected increase.

These are post-result, descriptive classifications from unadjusted pointwise
95% intervals. They show a visible pooled GAM-derivative pattern; they do not
demonstrate equivalence to a zero slope, an asymptote, a mechanistic ceiling,
or an association independent of site and collection period.
:::

## METRIC-011 bounded input reconciliation

On 2026-08-12, the sealed numerical-zero normalization in
`audit/decisions/l10_numerical_zero_normalization.md` changed eight primary
darkest-10-h-mean source cells from the floating-point residue
`4.163336342344337e-17` lx to exact zero: three near-eye cells and five chest
cells. The H07 reopening was therefore restricted to the L10 mean frames,
fits, diagnostics, declared sensitivities, leave-one-site-out checks, and the
BH fields in families containing the L10 slot. Historical V0 fits and all
non-L10 fits and raw tests remained frozen.

The bounded refit changed no sample count, diagnostic category, derivative
classification, transition grid point, conditional-AIC support category,
BH significance label, or three-decimal REPORT-008 value. The primary result
therefore remains six of nine near-eye and seven of nine chest patterns, with
the L10 mean classified as a derivative-defined plateau pattern at both
placements. Numerical derivative differences were limited to floating-point
roundoff (approximately `10^-15`).


## Revised ceiling assessment

After reviewing the original support-gated Stage 2 output, the owner reopened
H07-G1, H07-G9, and H07-G13 through decision `H07-002`. The scientific target
is now whether a plateau-like photoperiod association is visible in the pooled
data despite the known design limitations. The pooled local-support rule,
one-hour rule, and leave-one-site-out rule remain diagnostics but no longer
mask the derivative curve or determine eligibility.

For each metric and placement, the revised rule evaluates the first derivative
of `s(photoperiod_hours)` at 100 points spanning the exact recorded range. A
pattern begins when a pointwise detected increase is immediately followed by a
point whose 95% interval contains zero and every later point remains compatible
with zero through the maximum recorded photoperiod. The transition is reported
as the bracket between those two grid points. The primary implementation uses
central differences with forward/backward handling at the boundaries, a
0.01 h step, and unconditional covariance where available.

This decision was made after viewing Stage 2 support results and the intervals
are neither simultaneous over a curve nor adjusted across nine metrics.
Accordingly, the result is called a **derivative-defined plateau pattern**. It
is not an equivalence test: failure to detect a non-zero derivative does not
show that the slope is practically zero.

The registered latitude–photoperiod tensor remains structurally
non-identifiable because absolute latitude is determined by site. The adapted
photoperiod smooth has estimated concurvity of 0.9987–0.9989 with the remaining
model structure, so its whole-term p-values remain withheld. These limitations
do not suppress the requested descriptive pattern, but they prevent an
independent, site-general photoperiod or mechanistic interpretation.

## Approved analytical boundary

The owner approved H07 Stage 1 under decision `H07-001`, then amended the
ceiling and support gates under `H07-002`. All nine outcomes still enter
independently of H01 fitted results, p-values, or historical retention.
Near-eye measurements are primary; chest measurements are complementary.
Absolute latitude, civil photoperiod, site, participant nested in site, and
collection period remain the complete predictor and design boundary. No
temperature, weather, holiday, behavioural, clinical, or health-outcome
predictor was added.

The **gap-timing-unaware dataset** still passed the general 50%-per-hour and
80%-per-day coverage rules. Its name means that the timing of remaining
missing observations was not used for an additional metric-specific
adjustment; it does not mean that gaps, missingness, or coverage were ignored.
For contrast, the approved main input could be interpreted as a time-sensitive
primary metric dataset because its preparation uses the timing of remaining
missing observations when relevant. It is called the **primary dataset** from
this point onward.

# Implementation

## Exact fitted samples

The nine metrics have metric-specific complete rows. Participant-days equal
observations because the analytical unit is one participant-day. The primary
near-eye fits contain 139–141 participants, 655–816 participant-days, and all
nine sites. The complementary chest fits contain 153–154 participants,
743–902 participant-days, and eight sites; Tübingen has no chest data.

```{r}
#| label: main-samples

sample_display <- main_samples |>
  left_join(
    metric_registry |>
      select(metric_id, metric_order, manuscript_name),
    by = "metric_id"

  mutate(

    Placement = factor(
      placement_labels[placement],
      levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]

    Placement,

sample_display |>
```

## Exact model formulas and engine

All 162 main fits used exact `mgcv::gam(method = "REML")` under R 4.6.1.
There was no `bam()` fallback and no `discrete` argument. Every fitted model
converged according to the optimizer, although diagnostics can and do override
that numerical flag. The exact Wilkinson formulas supplied to the model are
shown from the persisted formula registry.

```{r}
#| label: exact-model-formulas
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false

exact_model_formulas <- formula_registry |>
  mutate(parsed_formula = lapply(formula, stats::as.formula))

stopifnot(
  all(vapply(
    exact_model_formulas$parsed_formula,
    inherits,
    logical(1),
    what = "formula"
  ))
)

for (index in seq_len(nrow(exact_model_formulas))) {
  cat(
    exact_model_formulas$model_id[[index]],
    ": ",
    paste(deparse(exact_model_formulas$parsed_formula[[index]]), collapse = " "),
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

The five registered formulas preserve the signed absolute-latitude–
photoperiod estimand and its predeclared comparisons. The four adapted
formulas estimate a narrower site-adjusted photoperiod curve and its basis and
site-representation checks. The adaptation cannot identify an independent
latitude association.

```{r}
#| label: model-fit-status

main_diagnostics |>
  count(model_id, fit_status, name = "Fits") |>
  mutate(
    `Model role` = recode(
      model_id,
      registered_null = "Registered null",
      registered_linear_surface = "Registered bilinear surface",
      registered_tensor = "Registered tensor",
      registered_tensor_expanded_basis = "Registered tensor, expanded basis",
      registered_tensor_fixed_site = "Registered tensor, fixed site",
      adapted_photoperiod_linear = "Adapted linear photoperiod",
      adapted_photoperiod_smooth = "Adapted smooth photoperiod",
      adapted_photoperiod_expanded_basis = "Adapted smooth, expanded basis",
      adapted_photoperiod_fixed_site = "Adapted smooth, fixed site"
    ),
    Status = recode(
      fit_status,
      PASS = "Numerically acceptable",
      WARN_CONCURVITY = "Converged; concurvity warning",
      FAIL_HESSIAN = "Failed Hessian gate"
    )
  ) |>
  select(`Model role`, Status, Fits) |>
  arrange(`Model role`, Status) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Main fit completion and diagnostic disposition",
    "Optimizer convergence alone did not release inference",
    font_size = 10
  ) |>
  cols_width(`Model role` ~ px(285), Status ~ px(240), Fits ~ px(70))
```

The sole Hessian failure was the expanded-basis adapted fit for the primary
near-eye longest continuous period above 250 lx melEDI. Its optimizer returned
convergence, but the minimum Hessian eigenvalue was negative; that comparison
is not interpreted.

# Revised derivative-defined plateau results

## Exact operational rule

The visible formula for the model supplying the derivative is:

```{r}
#| label: revised-derivative-formula
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false

revised_derivative_formula <- stats::as.formula(
  response_value ~ s(photoperiod_hours, k = 6, bs = "tp") +
    s(site, bs = "re") + s(site_participant, bs = "re")
)
revised_derivative_formula
```

The classification itself is:

```{r}
#| label: revised-derivative-rule
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false

revised_plateau_rule <- quote(
  previous_point_detected_increase &
    pointwise_compatible_with_zero &
    zero_compatible_to_recorded_end
)
revised_plateau_rule
```

Here, a detected increase means that the pointwise 95% derivative interval is
wholly above zero. The first subsequent zero-compatible point is accepted only
when every later point through the metric-specific maximum also has an
interval containing zero. The grid contains 100 points over the exact recorded
range. The derivative is the first derivative of the fitted photoperiod smooth
on its model/link scale; it is not a derivative of an isolated response-scale
mean.

## Primary near-eye results

```{r}
#| label: revised-near-eye-table

revised_primary <- revised_plateau_summary |>
  filter(.data$method_id == "REVISED_CENTRAL_UNCONDITIONAL_POINTWISE")

revised_table <- function(placement_value) {
  revised_primary |>
    filter(.data$placement == .env$placement_value) |>
    arrange(.data$metric_order) |>
    mutate(
      Pattern = if_else(.data$revised_plateau_pattern, "Yes", "No"),
      `Transition bracket` = if_else(
        .data$revised_plateau_pattern,
        sprintf(
          "%.2f–%.2f h",
          .data$plateau_transition_lower,
          .data$plateau_start
        ),
        "—"
      ),
      `Zero-compatible tail` = if_else(
        .data$revised_plateau_pattern,
        sprintf(
          "%.2f–%.2f h (%.2f h)",
          .data$plateau_start,
          .data$recorded_photoperiod_max,
          .data$plateau_tail_span_hours
        ),
        "—"
      ),
      `Reason when absent` = recode(
        .data$disposition,
        DERIVATIVE_DEFINED_PLATEAU_PATTERN = "—",
        NO_POINTWISE_DETECTED_PRIOR_INCREASE =
          "No earlier pointwise detected increase",
        POINTWISE_DETECTED_INCREASE_AT_RECORDED_END =
          "Detected increase persists at recorded end",
        LATER_POINTWISE_DETECTED_DECREASE =
          "Later pointwise detected decrease",
        NO_SUSTAINED_ZERO_COMPATIBLE_TAIL =
          "No zero-compatible tail through recorded end"
      )
    ) |>
    select(
      Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
      Pattern,
      `Transition bracket`,
      `Zero-compatible tail`,
      `Reason when absent`
    )
}

revised_table("near_eye") |>
  audit_gt(
    "Primary near-eye derivative-defined plateau patterns",
    "Central/boundary first derivative; unconditional pointwise 95% intervals; 100-point exact-range grid",
    font_size = 9
  ) |>
  cols_width(
    Metric ~ px(285),
    Pattern ~ px(70),
    `Transition bracket` ~ px(125),
    `Zero-compatible tail` ~ px(175),
    `Reason when absent` ~ px(275)
  )
```

Six near-eye metrics meet the revised rule. Mean melEDI transitions last, at
16.10–16.20 h. The remaining positive classifications begin between
14.24–14.35 h for melEDI dose and 15.17–15.27 h for brightest 10 h mean.
Each zero-compatible tail continues for at least 4.33 h to the recorded upper
boundary. The two low-light duration metrics have no earlier pointwise
detected increase, while longest continuous period above 250 lx melEDI remains
pointwise increasing at that boundary.

Each metric's response-scale fitted curve and model-scale derivative are shown
as a matched side-by-side pair over the same recorded photoperiod range. The
separate vertical axes are intentional: the left panel reports metric value,
whereas the right panel reports the derivative used by the classification.

```{r}
#| label: revised-near-eye-smooth-derivative-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Paired primary near-eye fitted curves and first derivatives from the adapted site- and participant-adjusted GAMs. Each row shows the fitted metric value on the response scale at left and the first derivative of the photoperiod smooth on the model/link scale at right. Grey ribbons are unconditional pointwise 95% intervals. A dashed blue line marks the positive-to-zero-compatible transition, and blue shading continues through the maximum recorded photoperiod when every later derivative interval contains zero. Rugs show metric-specific participant-day photoperiods. The classification is post-result and descriptive, with no curve-wide or cross-metric multiplicity control."
#| fig-alt: "Nine primary near-eye metric pairs are arranged in rows, with the fitted metric-value curve on the left and its first derivative on the right over the same civil-photoperiod range. ## Sensitivity to the V0 derivative settings
```

The revised primary calculation improves the finite-difference and covariance
handling but retains the requested pointwise logic. Repeating the rule with
V0's forward difference, `eps = 1e-7`, and conditional covariance gives the
same yes/no classification for all 18 metric-placement combinations. Boundary
locations are not equally stable: among classified patterns, the revised start
is 0.21–1.96 h earlier than under the V0 settings.

```{r}
#| label: revised-method-comparison

revised_method_comparison |>
  filter(.data$primary_plateau_pattern) |>
  mutate(
    Placement = factor(
      placement_labels[placement],
      levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]
    ),
    `Revised start` = sprintf("%.2f h", .data$primary_plateau_start),
    `V0-setting start` = sprintf("%.2f h", .data$comparison_plateau_start),
    `Revised minus V0` = sprintf("%.2f h", .data$boundary_difference_hours)
  ) |>
  arrange(Placement, .data$metric_order) |>
  select(
    Placement,
    Metric = .data$manuscript_name,
    `Revised start`,
    `V0-setting start`,
    `Revised minus V0`
  ) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Derivative-method sensitivity of the plateau boundary",
    subtitle = "The binary classification agrees for all 18 combinations; boundary timing remains method-dependent"
  ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(9),
    data_row.padding = px(3),
    heading.align = "left",
    table.width = pct(100)
  ) |>
  cols_width(Metric ~ px(300), everything() ~ px(145))
```

::: {.callout-warning title="What this revised result does and does not show"}
The visible derivative pattern answers the owner's simplified question. It
does not resolve the near-perfect concurvity of the photoperiod component, the
site–latitude identity, collection-period composition, sparse upper-tail site
representation, pointwise grid search, or site influence. A pointwise interval
containing zero means that a non-zero derivative was not detected at that grid
point; it does not show that the remaining slope is zero or negligible.
:::

# Association, shape, and diagnostic support

## Multiplicity and p-value disposition

Each placement contains four complete nine-metric families: registered
association, registered nonlinear shape, adapted association, and adapted
nonlinear shape. All eight family registries contain exactly nine rows. No
scientific p-value is displayed because the registered tests fail structural
latitude–site identifiability and the adapted tests fail the concurvity gate.
Consequently, REPORT-008 has no releasable p-value to format or bold.

```{r}
#| label: multiplicity-audit

main_family_audit |>
  mutate(
    Placement = placement_labels[sub("^primary__", "", run_id)],
    Scope = recode(
      analysis_scope,
      registered_tensor = "Registered tensor",
      adapted_photoperiod = "Adapted photoperiod"
    ),
    Test = recode(
      test_id,
      association = "Association",
      nonlinear_shape = "Nonlinear shape"
    ),
    `Observed / planned` = paste0(observed_family_n, " / ", planned_family_n)
  ) |>
  select(Placement, Scope, Test, `Observed / planned`, Status = status) |>
  arrange(factor(Placement, levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]), Scope, Test) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Nine-metric multiplicity families",
    "Rows remain in their planned family even when the p-value is withheld",
    font_size = 10
  ) |>
  cols_width(Placement ~ px(180), Scope ~ px(190), Test ~ px(145), everything() ~ px(120))
```

## Conditional AIC evidence

The table reports `AIC(full) - AIC(reduced)`. Negative values favour the full
model conditionally; positive values favour the reduced model. For association
the full model is the adapted smooth and the reduced model is the null. For
shape the full model is the adapted smooth and the reduced model is the linear
photoperiod model. These mixed AIC patterns are not significance tests and do
not establish a ceiling.

```{r}
#| label: adapted-aic-evidence

adapted_aic <- main_tests |>
  filter(analysis_scope == "adapted_photoperiod") |>
  select(
    run_id,
    metric_order,
    manuscript_name,
    test_id,
    delta_aic_full_minus_reduced,
    conditional_aic_support
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = test_id,
    values_from = c(
      delta_aic_full_minus_reduced,
      conditional_aic_support
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Placement = factor(
      placement_labels[sub("^primary__", "", run_id)],
      levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]
    ),
    `Association ΔAIC` = sprintf(
      "%.2f",
      delta_aic_full_minus_reduced_association
    ),
    `Shape ΔAIC` = sprintf(
      "%.2f",
      delta_aic_full_minus_reduced_nonlinear_shape
    ),
    `Association reading` = recode(
      conditional_aic_support_association,
      FULL_LOWER_BY_MORE_THAN_2 = "Full lower by >2",
      FULL_LOWER_BY_0_TO_2 = "Full lower by 0–2",
      REDUCED_LOWER = "Reduced lower"
    ),
    `Shape reading` = recode(
      conditional_aic_support_nonlinear_shape,
      FULL_LOWER_BY_MORE_THAN_2 = "Full lower by >2",
      FULL_LOWER_BY_0_TO_2 = "Full lower by 0–2",
      REDUCED_LOWER = "Reduced lower"
    ),
    `P-value status` = "Withheld — concurvity"
  ) |>
  arrange(Placement, metric_order) |>
  select(
    Placement,
    Metric = manuscript_name,
    `Association ΔAIC`,
    `Association reading`,
    `Shape ΔAIC`,
    `Shape reading`,
    `P-value status`
  )

adapted_aic |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Adapted photoperiod conditional AIC comparisons",
    subtitle = "Secondary relative-support evidence only; no p-value or ceiling decision"
  ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(9),
    data_row.padding = px(3),
    heading.align = "left",
    table.width = pct(100)
  ) |>
  cols_width(Metric ~ px(255), everything() ~ px(130))
```

## Former pooled-support rule as a design diagnostic

The support grid required at least three represented sites, 20 participants,
50 participant-days, and no site contributing more than 60% locally. Near-eye
fits passed this pooled rule at only four or five isolated grid points between
10.6 and 11.0 h. The accepted continuous-run algorithm found no sustained
one-hour interval. Chest fits passed the pooled rule at no grid point. No
metric retained any point after all site omissions.

Under H07-002 these facts describe cross-site overlap and transportability;
they no longer censor the derivative grid or veto the requested pooled-data
classification. The endpoint table and grey/blue overlays are retained to
make the superseded gate and its consequence auditable. Intervals are
pointwise 95% confidence intervals from the adapted fit and are not
simultaneous.

```{r}
#| label: supported-endpoints

near_supported <- main_curve_points |>
  filter(placement == "near_eye", pooled_eligible) |>
  group_by(metric_id, metric_order, manuscript_name) |>
  arrange(photoperiod_hours, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    `Eligible points` = n(),
    `Lower supported grid point` = first(photoperiod_hours),
    lower_estimate = first(response_estimate),
    lower_ci = first(response_lower_pointwise),
    lower_hi = first(response_upper_pointwise),
    `Upper supported grid point` = last(photoperiod_hours),
    upper_estimate = last(response_estimate),
    upper_ci = last(response_lower_pointwise),
    upper_hi = last(response_upper_pointwise),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    metric_registry |>
      select(metric_id, display_unit),
    by = "metric_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    `Lower estimate (95% CI)` = format_ci(
      lower_estimate,
      lower_ci,
      lower_hi
    ),
    `Upper estimate (95% CI)` = format_ci(
      upper_estimate,
      upper_ci,
      upper_hi
    ),
    `Lower grid` = sprintf("%.1f h", `Lower supported grid point`),
    `Upper grid` = sprintf("%.1f h", `Upper supported grid point`),
    Unit = display_unit,
    `LOSO-eligible points` = 0L
  ) |>
  arrange(metric_order) |>
  select(
    Metric = manuscript_name,
    `Eligible points`,
    `Lower grid`,
    `Lower estimate (95% CI)`,
    `Upper grid`,
    `Upper estimate (95% CI)`,
    Unit,
    `LOSO-eligible points`
  )

near_supported |>
  audit_gt(
    "Former pooled-support gate: isolated near-eye grid points",
    "Diagnostic under H07-002; four or five points do not form the former continuous run and all LOSO counts are zero",
    font_size = 9
  ) |>
  cols_width(
    Metric ~ px(250),
    `Lower estimate (95% CI)` ~ px(165),
    `Upper estimate (95% CI)` ~ px(165),
    everything() ~ px(95)
  )
```

# Diagnostics

## Latitude, site, participant, and collection period

Each site has one absolute latitude. The primary near-eye data therefore have
nine site latitudes and the chest data eight; latitude is not replicated
independently within site. Collection periods differ by site, and several
sites cover narrow or disjoint photoperiod regions. Site, latitude,
photoperiod, and collection period cannot be interpreted as separable effects.

The site table shows the range across metric-specific samples. Its ordering
and names follow the submitted manuscript display registry.

```{r}
#| label: site-support

site_support_display <- main_site_support |>
  group_by(placement, site) |>
  summarise(
    participant_min = min(participants),
    participant_max = max(participants),
    day_min = min(participant_days),
    day_max = max(participant_days),
    first_date = min(first_date),
    last_date = max(last_date),
    abs_latitude_deg = first(abs_latitude_deg),
    photoperiod_min = min(photoperiod_min),
    photoperiod_max = max(photoperiod_max),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(site_display, by = "site") |>
  mutate(
    Placement = factor(
      placement_labels[placement],
      levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]
    ),
    Site = factor(display_name, levels = site_display$display_name),
    Participants = if_else(
      participant_min == participant_max,
      as.character(participant_min),
      paste0(participant_min, "–", participant_max)
    ),
    `Participant-days` = if_else(
      day_min == day_max,
      as.character(day_min),
      paste0(day_min, "–", day_max)
    ),
    `Collection period` = paste(first_date, "to", last_date),
    `Absolute latitude` = sprintf("%.1f°", abs_latitude_deg),
    `Photoperiod range` = sprintf(
      "%.2f–%.2f h",
      photoperiod_min,
      photoperiod_max
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(Placement, Site) |>
  select(
    Placement,
    Site,
    Participants,
    `Participant-days`,
    `Collection period`,
    `Absolute latitude`,
    `Photoperiod range`
  )

site_support_display |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Metric-specific site support and collection periods",
    subtitle = "Ranges reflect metric-specific complete rows; absolute latitude is constant within site"
  ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(9),
    data_row.padding = px(3),
    heading.align = "left",
    table.width = pct(100)
  ) |>
  cols_width(
    Site ~ px(150),
    `Collection period` ~ px(185),
    everything() ~ px(115)
  )
```

The decisive support limitation is visible in the table: Kumasi and San José
cover narrow photoperiod bands, Munich covers only a short high-photoperiod
period, Tübingen appears only near eye, and the northern sites cover broad but
different collection windows. Repeated participant-days increase precision
within these cells but do not create independent latitude or site replication.

## Concurvity, basis, and numerical diagnostics

For all 18 adapted smooth fits, the estimated worst concurvity for the target
photoperiod smooth is 0.9987–0.9989. Pairwise decomposition identifies the
participant random-effect smooth as the dominant supplier (0.9985–0.9988);
the site random-effect smooth contributes approximately 0.483–0.550. This is
not a minor warning: the participant structure can nearly reproduce the
photoperiod smooth, so approximate whole-term tests are withheld.

Four adapted fits trigger the default basis-dimension check. The expanded-
basis comparison stays in the same direction over the few supported near-eye
points for eight metrics; the longest-period expanded fit fails the Hessian
gate. None of the expanded or fixed-site alternatives resolves concurvity.

```{r}
#| label: adapted-diagnostics

adapted_diagnostics <- main_diagnostics |>
  filter(model_id == "adapted_photoperiod_smooth") |>
  left_join(
    metric_registry |>
      select(metric_id, metric_order, manuscript_name),
    by = "metric_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Placement = factor(
      placement_labels[sub("^primary__", "", run_id)],
      levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]
    ),
    `Smooth edf` = sprintf("%.2f", smooth_edf),
    `k-index` = sprintf("%.3f", k_index),
    `Basis check` = if_else(k_p_value < 0.05, "Flagged", "Not flagged"),
    `Estimated concurvity` = sprintf("%.4f", concurvity_estimate),
    `Pooled day-lag 1` = sprintf("%+.3f", pooled_consecutive_day_lag1),
    `Temporal gate` = "Pass",
    `Inference` = "Withheld"
  ) |>
  arrange(Placement, metric_order) |>
  select(
    Placement,
    Metric = manuscript_name,
    `Smooth edf`,
    `k-index`,
    `Basis check`,
    `Estimated concurvity`,
    `Pooled day-lag 1`,
    `Temporal gate`,
    Inference
  )

adapted_diagnostics |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Adapted smooth diagnostics",
    subtitle = "Diagnostic p-values are used only to flag basis checks; scientific p-values remain withheld"
  ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(9),
    data_row.padding = px(3),
    heading.align = "left",
    table.width = pct(100)
  ) |>
  cols_width(Metric ~ px(250), everything() ~ px(105))
```

## Temporal dependence

All 162 main fits pass the prespecified descriptive dependence gate. The
largest absolute pooled consecutive-day lag-1 correlation is
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(main_diagnostics$pooled_consecutive_day_lag1), na.rm = TRUE))`,
below the 0.30 trigger. No AR(1) or participant-cluster correction is added.
Passing this gate does not repair the cross-site or concurvity failures.

## Residual distributions and physical bounds

Residual checks show response-specific limitations rather than one uniform
failure. Across placements, the Pearson-residual normal-quantile correlation
ranges from approximately 0.952 to 0.998, residual excess kurtosis reaches
8.35, and the maximum absolute fitted-versus-absolute-residual correlation is
0.348. The strongest tail or shape departures occur for darkest 10 h mean,
melEDI dose, mean melEDI, brightest 10 h mean, and the sleep-environment
duration. These patterns make Gaussian-response intervals provisional where
applicable; they do not justify a result-selected family switch.

No observed metric value is negative and no observed duration exceeds 24 h.
After correcting the H07-local fitted-range diagnostic so that `fitted.gam()`
Tweedie response-scale values are not exponentiated twice, all adapted-fit
duration fitted values span 0.15–9.62 h. A pointwise lower curve bound for complementary chest
darkest 10 h mean crosses zero outside any supported region; the point
estimate does not. This reinforces the decision not to interpret chest curves
outside support.

```{r}
#| label: residual-summary

residual_display <- main_residuals |>
  group_by(placement) |>
  summarise(
    `QQ correlation range` = sprintf(
      "%.3f–%.3f",
      min(normal_qq_correlation),
      max(normal_qq_correlation)
    ),
    `Skewness range` = sprintf(
      "%+.2f to %+.2f",
      min(residual_skewness),
      max(residual_skewness)
    ),
    `Maximum excess kurtosis` = sprintf("%.2f", max(residual_excess_kurtosis)),
    `Maximum |cor(fitted, |residual|)|` = sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      max(abs(fitted_absolute_residual_correlation))
    ),
    `Maximum proportion |Pearson| > 3` = sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      max(proportion_abs_pearson_above_3)
    ),
    `Observed negative values` = sum(observed_negative),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Placement = factor(
      placement_labels[placement],
      levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(Placement) |>
  select(-placement)

residual_display |>
  audit_gt(
    "Residual-distribution summary",
    "Pearson residuals from the adapted smooth fits",
    font_size = 9
  ) |>
  cols_width(Placement ~ px(175), everything() ~ px(145))
```

## Tweedie 100-simulation pilot

The three duration metrics assigned estimated-power Tweedie models received
the approved 100-simulation distribution pilot. Time above 1,000 lx melEDI
has compatible zero counts and upper tails. Time above 250 lx melEDI during
wake has compatible zero counts and 95th percentiles, although its observed
maximum is lighter than the pilot envelope. The sleep-environment metric has
four observed zero days in each placement, while the analytic expectation is
less than 0.0001 and all 100 simulations produce zero zeros. Its fitted power
is also near the lower boundary. That common family fails its zero-mass gate.

No post-hoc alternative model has been fitted. The recommended Stage 2
disposition is to retain this metric as descriptive and non-inferential rather
than reopen the common-family contract when all H07 association tests are
already withheld for design reasons.

```{r}
#| label: tweedie-pilot

tweedie_display <- tweedie_pilot |>
  mutate(
    Placement = factor(
      placement_labels[placement],
      levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]
    ),
    Power = sprintf("%.3f", power),
    `Observed zeros` = observed_zero_count,
    `Analytic expected zeros` = if_else(
      analytic_expected_zero_count < 0.001,
      "<0.001",
      sprintf("%.2f", analytic_expected_zero_count)
    ),
    `100-run zero envelope` = paste0(
      sprintf("%.1f", simulated_zero_lower),
      "–",
      sprintf("%.1f", simulated_zero_upper)
    ),
    `Observed / pilot positive 95th percentile` = paste0(
      sprintf("%.2f", observed_positive_q95),
      " / ",
      sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", simulated_positive_q95_lower, simulated_positive_q95_upper)
    ),
    Reading = case_when(
      metric_id == "duration_below_1_sleep_environment" ~
        "Fails zero-mass gate",
      metric_id == "duration_above_250_wake" ~
        "Zero mass and 95th percentile compatible; maximum lighter",
      TRUE ~ "Zero mass and upper tail compatible"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(Placement, metric_order) |>
  select(
    Placement,
    Metric = manuscript_name,
    Power,
    `Observed zeros`,
    `Analytic expected zeros`,
    `100-run zero envelope`,
    `Observed / pilot positive 95th percentile`,
    Reading
  )

tweedie_display |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Placement") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Tweedie distribution pilot",
    subtitle = "100 simulations only; pilot is diagnostic, not inferential or manuscript-ready"
  ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(9),
    data_row.padding = px(3),
    heading.align = "left",
    table.width = pct(100)
  ) |>
  cols_width(Metric ~ px(245), Reading ~ px(290), everything() ~ px(125))
```

# Sensitivity and influence analyses

## Exact sensitivity samples

The paired placement branch uses only participant-days with both placements:
110–112 participants, 505–643 participant-days, and eight sites, depending on
metric. The gap-timing-unaware branch contains 140–141 near-eye participants
and 755–811 participant-days, and 153–154 chest participants and 839–897
participant-days. Exact preparation-common rows are evaluated separately from
the total dataset difference.

The exactly identified longest-period sensitivity contains 132 participants
and 500 participant-days near eye and 150 participants and 564 participant-
days at the chest. The observed and corrected dose comparison uses the same
141 participants and 761 participant-days near eye and 154 participants and
851 participant-days at the chest.

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-samples

sensitivity_sample_display <- sensitivity_samples |>
  left_join(
    sensitivity_registry |>
      select(run_id, sensitivity, placement),
    by = "run_id",
    suffix = c("", ".registry")
  ) |>
  group_by(sensitivity, placement) |>
  summarise(
    Participants = range_cell(participants),
    `Participant-days` = range_cell(participant_days),
    Observations = range_cell(observations),
    Sites = range_cell(sites),
    `Collection period` = paste(min(first_date), "to", max(last_date)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Sensitivity = recode(
      sensitivity,
      paired_common_placement = "Paired/common placement",
      gap_timing_unaware = "Gap-timing-unaware dataset",
```

## Revised derivative-pattern sensitivity

The simplified classification is not uniformly stable across the already
approved data branches. The gap-timing-unaware dataset reproduces all nine
near-eye classifications and eight of nine chest classifications; chest
melEDI dose loses its main-data pattern. The exact preparation-common branches
reproduce all near-eye classifications, while time below 1 lx melEDI during
sleep loses its chest classification in both common-row scenarios. Corrected
and observed dose agree on their common sample at both placements.

The paired/common placement sample is the most consequential change. Only
four of nine near-eye classifications agree with the main all-available
analysis: the patterns for brightest and darkest 10 h means, both bright-light
duration metrics, and melEDI dose are no longer detected. Six of nine chest
classifications agree; the sleep-environment duration, longest-period, and
dose patterns disappear. In the exactly identified longest-period sensitivity,
near eye changes from no pattern to a transition at 15.38–15.48 h.


## Former support-restricted curve comparisons

These H07-001 curve comparisons are retained as diagnostics. All 58 remain
inferentially non-estimable
because every relevant adapted smooth has the concurvity warning. Paired
placement and exactly identified longest-period comparisons have no common
pooled support. All chest preparation and dose comparisons also have no
common pooled support.

For near eye, the two preparation comparisons retain the same direction over
only four or five isolated points for all nine metrics. Corrected and observed
melEDI dose also retain the same direction over four points, with maximum
absolute log ratio 0.031. No scientific magnitude threshold was fixed, so
these are descriptive direction checks, not stability or equivalence claims.
H07-002's full-range pointwise derivative classification is summarized
separately above.

## Basis and site representation

Under the former support-restricted comparison, 17 of 18 near-eye alternative
curves have the same
direction as the main curve over the few pooled-eligible points. The one
exception is not a direction reversal: the expanded-basis longest-period fit
fails the Hessian gate. The fixed-site equal-site average can shift curve
magnitude substantially—for example maximum absolute log ratios of 0.353 for
melEDI dose and 0.292 for longest continuous period—while preserving the
direction over those isolated points. Chest has no pooled-supported point for
any model-form comparison. No materiality threshold was fixed, and every
alternative smooth still has a concurvity warning.

Applying H07-002's full-range derivative rule shows two classification
changes. The expanded-basis chest model no longer classifies time below 1 lx
melEDI during sleep; its near-eye longest-period fit remains unavailable after
the Hessian failure. The fixed-site representation also removes that chest
sleep-environment classification and adds a near-eye longest-period pattern at
14.86–14.96 h. Thus 16 of 17 evaluable expanded-basis classifications and 16
of 18 fixed-site classifications agree with the main model.

## Leave-one-site-out influence

All 153 leave-one-site-out fits converge, and all retain the concurvity
warning. No metric has full support under the superseded leave-one-site-out
eligibility rule. H07-002 instead treats each omission as an influence check
over that omitted dataset's complete recorded photoperiod range.

Near-eye mean melEDI and both low-light duration classifications agree after
all nine omissions. For five primary near-eye plateau patterns, eight of nine
omissions retain the classification; omitting Munich is the discordant case.
The main near-eye longest-period result is especially site-sensitive: four of
nine omissions create a pattern that is absent in the full fit. At the chest,
mean melEDI, time above 1,000 lx melEDI, and time below 10 lx melEDI before
sleep agree after all eight omissions. Other chest classifications are more
site-sensitive; the sleep-environment pattern remains after only three of
eight omissions.

These findings do not veto the requested pooled-data classification, but they
show that several patterns and their transition hours depend on which sites
define the photoperiod curve. They do not identify a causal site effect.

# H11 implementation comparison

H11's difficulty does not imply that H07 should use `discrete = FALSE`. H11
originally planned ML/non-discrete comparisons for large half-hourly Gaussian
models with an AR(1) boundary structure. That branch produced no accepted
checkpoint and was replaced by inference from an existing fREML/discrete fit
using AR-whitened participant-cluster CR1 covariance. H11's method targets a
complete 24-hour sex-difference curve under serial correlation.

H07 instead has one participant-day row per outcome, exact `gam(REML)` fits
completed quickly, and the temporal trigger was not crossed. Its remaining
limitations are that latitude is determined by site, photoperiod is nearly
reproduced by participant structure, and cross-site joint support is sparse.
Neither `bam(discrete = FALSE)` nor H11's CR1 covariance changes those design
facts. The computational choice is therefore retained: exact `gam(REML)`, no
`bam()` fallback, no ML branch, and no transferred CR1 procedure. H07-002
changes the descriptive derivative estimand, not the fitting engine.

# Reproduction of the V0 GAM-derivative method

## Exact V0 specification

V0 first selected outcome-placement pairs using `AIC(full) - AIC(null) < -2`.
It fitted Gaussian `log10(value + 0.1)` models with `mgcv::bam()`, fREML,
`discrete = TRUE`, and ten threads. It then used a 100-point forward derivative
with `eps = 1e-7`, a conditional covariance matrix, and pointwise 95%
confidence limits. The last grid point with a positive lower limit became the
reported boundary.

```{r}
#| label: v0-formulas
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false

for (index in seq_len(nrow(v0_formulas))) {
  cat(
    v0_formulas$formula_id[[index]],
    ": ",
    v0_formulas$formula[[index]],
    " | engine = ",
    v0_formulas$engine[[index]],
    ", method = ",
    v0_formulas$method[[index]],
    ", discrete = ",
    v0_formulas$discrete[[index]],
    ", nthreads = ",
    v0_formulas$nthreads[[index]],
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

## Numeric reconstruction

All ten historical retain/exclude decisions reproduce. Every available
rendered ΔAIC value agrees within its displayed rounding; four excluded rows
had no printed numeric ΔAIC to compare. V0 retained six of eight near-eye
candidates and four of six chest candidates. It did not assess all nine
metrics per placement.

The reconstructed boundary reaches the maximum observed photoperiod (20.52 h)
for near-eye longest continuous period and melEDI dose, and for chest
brightest 10 h mean and melEDI dose. These edge cases fail H07-002 because
there is no subsequent zero-compatible pointwise tail.

Applying H07-002's added through-the-recorded-end requirement to the complete
V0 derivative curves classifies eight of the 14 V0 candidate combinations and
six of the ten historically AIC-retained combinations. This confirms that the
revised rule is not merely a relabelling of V0's last-positive point.

# Pointwise rule and optional simultaneous-band gate

H07-002's requested classification uses the first derivative of the fitted
photoperiod smooth, analytic pointwise 95% intervals, and no simulation. It
therefore does not require production computation.

Before H07-002, the audit completed a 100-draw pilot for simultaneous bands of
the full response prediction over only the former pooled-eligible grid. That
pilot is retained below as historical implementation evidence. It is not the
current derivative estimand and does not cover the full recorded range; chest
has no point under that former mask.

Near-eye pilot critical values range from 1.69 to 2.38 over four or five
isolated eligible points. Chest has no eligible point, so no simultaneous
critical value can be calculated. Projected 10,000-draw runtime is 0.9–1.9 s
per metric. These values cannot be reused as a full-range simultaneous band
for the revised rule.

```{r}
#| label: derivative-pilot-figure
#| fig-cap: "Historical H07-001 near-eye derivative validation pilot. Blue ribbons are pointwise 95% intervals and red dashed lines are 100-draw pilot simultaneous bands for full response-scale derivatives over the former isolated pooled-eligible points. H07-002 uses the full-range smooth-derivative displays above instead."
#| fig-alt: "Nine panels show response-scale photoperiod derivatives only from 10.6 to 11.0 hours. Blue lines and pale pointwise confidence bands are accompanied by red dashed 100-draw pilot simultaneous limits. Some derivatives are positive, some negative, and some cross zero, but the region is isolated and not leave-one-site-out stable."
#| out-width: "100%"

knitr::include_graphics(h07_figure_path("H07_derivative_pilot_near_eye.png"))
```

[Source CSV for the derivative pilot](../../../artifacts/09_tables/H07/H07_main_derivative_pilot_points.csv)

```{r}
#| label: derivative-pilot-runtime

derivative_runtime |>
  group_by(placement) |>
  summarise(
    Metrics = n(),
    `Pilot draws per metric` = range_cell(draws),
    `Eligible grid points` = range_cell(eligible_grid_points),
    `Pilot critical-value range` = if_else(
      any(is.finite(simultaneous_critical_pilot)),
      sprintf(
        "%.2f–%.2f",
        min(simultaneous_critical_pilot, na.rm = TRUE),
        max(simultaneous_critical_pilot, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      "Not estimable"
    ),
    `Projected 10,000-draw runtime` = sprintf(
      "%.1f–%.1f s per metric",
      min(projected_10000_seconds),
      max(projected_10000_seconds)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Placement = factor(
      placement_labels[placement],
      levels = placement_labels[placement_levels]
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(Placement) |>
  select(-placement) |>
  audit_gt(
    "Historical H07-001 simultaneous-band pilot and runtime projection",
    "No production draw has been run; a revised full-range pilot would be required before any H07-002 simultaneous sensitivity",
    font_size = 10
  ) |>
  cols_width(Placement ~ px(180), `Projected 10,000-draw runtime` ~ px(210), everything() ~ px(145))
```

The current recommendation remains **do not run production derivative
draws** because the owner requested the simpler pointwise rule. If a stricter
curve-wide sensitivity is desired, it first requires a new 100-draw pilot over
the complete metric-specific range, followed by separate approval for the
projected production run. Even a simultaneous zero-compatible tail would not
be an equivalence test.

# Reproducibility and audit trail

Stage 2 fitted 162 main models, 234 sensitivity models, 153 leave-one-site-out
models, and 28 V0 full/null models. All model frames, fit checkpoints,
diagnostics, tests, support grids, curve sources, and run registries are
persisted in H07-owned artifact paths. No production bootstrap or simulation
was run; only the two approved 100-replicate pilots were executed. H07-002
added derivative extraction from existing checkpoints for 18 main, 78 data
sensitivity, 36 model-form, 153 leave-one-site-out, and 14 V0 candidate
combinations. It did not refit a model or run a simulation.

# Revised Stage 2 author approval gate

Stage 2 stops here. Approve or revise each item before any Stage 3 report or
production computation:

1. **H07-S2R-001 — inferential disposition:** accept that registered H07 is
   non-identifiable because absolute latitude is determined by site, and that
   adapted association and shape p-values are withheld because of extreme
   concurvity. These remain interpretation limitations rather than gates that
   suppress H07-002's descriptive derivative pattern.
2. **H07-S2R-002 — revised plateau result:** accept the post-result pointwise
   definition and the resulting six-of-nine primary near-eye and seven-of-nine
   complementary chest classifications, with the exact transition brackets
   and absence reasons shown above. Use “derivative-defined plateau pattern”
   and do not translate it into equivalence, an asymptote, a mechanistic
   ceiling, or a causal effect.
3. **H07-S2R-003 — sensitivity and influence:** accept that the V0 derivative
   settings preserve all 18 main yes/no classifications but shift boundaries;
   paired/common samples, model form, exact-period data, and site omission
   change several classifications. Treat these as visible limitations rather
   than exclusion rules.
4. **H07-S2R-004 — distributional disposition:** accept the 100-simulation
   finding that the Tweedie family fails the sleep-environment zero-mass gate,
   retain that metric as descriptive and non-inferential, and do not add a
   post-hoc family solely for H07.
5. **H07-S2R-005 — H11 comparison:** accept exact `gam(REML)` as fitted, with no
   `bam(discrete = FALSE)` branch and no transferred H11 CR1 method, because
   neither changes H07's site, latitude, photoperiod, or collection-period
   structure.
6. **H07-S2R-006 — V0 comparison:** accept the exact AIC reproduction, the
   distinction between V0's last detected increase and H07-002's required
   zero-compatible tail, and the finding that six of ten historically retained
   V0 combinations meet the added rule.
7. **H07-S2R-007 — production decision:** approve the recommendation to run no
   production simultaneous derivative draw. A stricter full-range curve-wide
   sensitivity would first require a new 100-draw pilot and then separate
   production approval.
8. **H07-S2R-008 — transition:** approve this revised Stage 2 result package
   for Stage 3 reader-facing reporting only after H07-S2R-001 through
   H07-S2R-007 are fixed.
